data.body:
RP-03 retry ownership approved (2026-08-17).

The maintainer approved a two-level pattern suitable for future GitHub Issues, Linear, and other tracker adapters without adding those adapters to RP-03 scope. Concrete adapters own the only physical request-replay loop, request/subprocess timeouts and cleanup, native SDK retry configuration, provider error/header decoding, and physical-attempt evidence. The backend-neutral reconciler owns operation intent/postconditions, `commit_unknown`, write-ahead/lifecycle recovery, re-observation and re-planning, dependency deferral, long-delay scheduling, the scoped finite-pass fuse, and exact ticket/pass outcomes. `jira_family` may contain only pure Cloud/DC-shared classification/value behavior; it owns no retry loop, sleep, budget, clock, counter, or fuse.

Physical replay uses a two-key authorization rule: the core must declare the logical operation/postcondition replayable, and the concrete adapter must prove its exact request was not applied, provider-idempotent, or freshly/deterministically deduplicated. Either proof missing yields `commit_unknown` for core re-observation. Compound adapter methods are not one replay unit; late-leg failure preserves confirmed earlier effects and triggers re-observation rather than repeating the whole method. Configurable SDK retries are disabled (`jira.JIRA(max_retries=0)`); opaque CLI-native retries are never multiplied by an outer Rebar write retry. Physical attempts and logical operations are separate accounting dimensions.

The approved addendum is saved in `.joe-janitor/rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md` and `.joe-janitor/rp03-outbound-lifecycle-research.md`. This work did not touch the in-flight RP-04 epic, stories, worktree, or implementation state. Next RP-03 decision: calibrate inline physical retry/defer budgets and finite-pass fuse thresholds.
